clue.text: Vehicle in street, a crock, reconditioned

indicators.note: an old banger that is reconditioned is rebuilt, so the letters of 'a crock' are put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: An old wreck parked on the road has been done up to run again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reconditioned' is the anagram signal for 'a crock'; a crock is an old, broken-down car, so the surface keeps a motoring scene.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a car modified for a racing sport where cars may collide, so it is a type of vehicle.

clue.text: Touched up a des res abroad, below Cape

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece below another comes after it

parts.note: C is the map abbreviation for cape

indicators.note: abroad can mean astray or all over the place, so the letters of 'a des res' are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A desirable residence overseas, beneath a headland, has been given some cosmetic improvement by the estate agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' rearranges A DES RES into ARESSED, which goes below C. A des res is British estate-agent slang for a desirable residence.
explanation.definitionFit: Touched up is informal for fondled in an unwelcome way, a stroking sense close to the answer.

clue.text: Sample of fakir's cherry brandy

indicators.note: Sample of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A holy man offers a taste of his cherry spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Kirsch is a clear spirit distilled from cherries, a fruit brandy; the word 'cherry' in the clue also hints at it.

clue.text: Large bath as focal point — too much inside

indicators.note: inside says the letters for 'too much' sit within the word for focal point

parts.note: a hub is the centre or focal point of activity
OTT is short for over the top, meaning excessive

explanation.surface: A big tub makes the centrepiece of a room, perhaps rather excessive.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT is British shorthand for over the top; 'inside' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A heated outdoor tub big enough for several people to soak in together is a large bath.

clue.text: Musical heroine, Greek character, street singer

parts.note: Maria is the heroine of The Sound of Music (and of West Side Story)
chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A list of performers: a stage heroine, a Greek figure and a busker.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mexican band musician who often plays and sings in streets and squares is a street singer.

clue.text: Shelter made from loose stones found on bottom of tarn

parts.note: scree is a mass of loose stones on a mountainside

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A walker's shelter is built from loose rocks gathered at the bottom of a mountain lake.
explanation.walkthrough: A tarn is a small mountain lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A partition or barrier that gives protection from view or wind is a shelter.

clue.text: Work in outskirts of Tobruk on a very good film

indicators.note: in places the work between the outer letters of Tobruk
outskirts are the edges, so only the first and last letters of Tobruk are used

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work
pi, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for very good

explanation.surface: A film set on the edge of Tobruk earns a glowing review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'outskirts of' work together: the opus sits between the edge letters of Tobruk, a port in Libya.
explanation.definitionFit: Topkapi is a 1964 heist caper movie about stealing a jewelled dagger from an Istanbul palace museum.

clue.text: Artist under pressure to visit art museum

indicators.note: in a down clue, the artist placed under pressure follows it

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
RA is a Royal Academician, a recognised artist
to do a place is to visit it as a tourist, as in doing Paris

explanation.surface: A painter is pushed into touring a gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prado in Madrid is one of the world's great galleries of paintings.

clue.text: Lacking imagination, Ms Klebb in film?

indicators.note: in puts the first name inside the word for film

parts.note: pic is informal for a motion picture
Rosa Klebb is the villain of the Bond film From Russia with Love

explanation.surface: A dull Bond villain in a movie, unimaginatively written.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that Ms Klebb stands for her first name, not a definition of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dull and matter-of-fact, without flair or poetry, lacks imagination.

clue.text: Missile's power staggered sailor

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power

indicators.note: a staggering man reels about, so the letters of 'sailor' lurch into a new order

explanation.surface: A drunken seaman reels under the force of a rocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staggered' makes OLARIS from SAILOR; 'Missile's' is a contraction of 'Missile is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Polaris was a US submarine-launched ballistic nuclear weapon also used by the Royal Navy.

clue.text: Follow suit, holding hearts

indicators.note: holding means the word for suit wraps around the letter for hearts

parts.note: a suit is a lawsuit, a legal case
H is the card-game abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: A card player follows suit while keeping hold of hearts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Follow suit' looks like one card-table phrase; 'Follow' alone is the definition and 'suit' is a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: To pursue or run after someone is to follow them.

clue.text: Game to Israel, I suspect

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious or not right, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone guesses which country a match is heading to.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-player card or peg game, patience in Britain, is a game.

clue.text: A problem wearing religious symbols? Take an irrevocable step

indicators.note: wearing means the problem is clothed by the two symbols placed around it

parts.note: a cross is a Christian symbol
an icon is a sacred image
'the rub' means the difficulty, as in Hamlet's 'there's the rub'

explanation.surface: A cleric's dilemma about putting on crosses and icons before making a decision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'religious symbols' supplies two pieces, and 'wearing' has them around the problem; the question mark covers that double duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar's crossing of a river into Italy began civil war, so the idiom means committing to a point of no return.

clue.text: 6, rose-red possibly

indicators.note: possibly says these letters are one possible arrangement of something else

explanation.surface: A colour description that might apply to the screen across a church.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition '6' points to the answer of 6 Down.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is an ornamental partition behind a church altar, so it is a kind of 6 Down.

clue.text: Enjoys sauces etc

definitions.meaning: to savour or take pleasure in something
pickles, chutneys and other spicy accompaniments to food

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for taking delight in something and a plural noun for tangy condiments.

clue.text: Withdraw with slight injury

definitions.meaning: to pull a horse or competitor out of an event
a small mark or graze on the skin

explanation.surface: An athlete pulls out of a race because of a minor wound.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both pulling out of a contest and a minor graze made by a claw or thorn.

clue.text: Anecdotes from leader of Scottish Conservatives

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: Tories are members of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Tales told by the head of the Scottish Tory party.
explanation.walkthrough: Tories is the everyday name for Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Short amusing accounts of incidents are tales or narratives.

clue.text: Neglect? Ring embassy

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
a diplomatic mission is an embassy

explanation.surface: A worried call to an embassy about some failure of duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A failure to do something that should have been done is a form of negligence.

clue.text: Bottle party in bar

indicators.note: in places the group inside the word for bar

parts.note: to stop is to bar or block
a crew is a group or party of people

explanation.surface: A bottle is taken to a party in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle party' and 'bar' read as a drinks scene; 'party' is a group of people and 'bar' a verb meaning block.
explanation.definitionFit: A container with a threaded lid is a kind of bottle; the term names the vessel by its cap.

clue.text: Vet, Leo, with derringer, shot dog

indicators.note: shot means ruined or wrecked, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A vet named Leo used a small pistol to put down a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like the derringer firing, but it is the anagram signal; a derringer is a small pistol.
explanation.definitionFit: A popular gun-dog breed with a gold coat, bred to fetch game, is a dog.

clue.text: Influenza under control? Almost

indicators.note: almost means the word stops just short of its final letter

parts.note: something gripped is firmly held and so under control

explanation.surface: A flu outbreak has nearly been contained.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for flu, la grippe, is used in English for influenza.

clue.text: Raised in crocodile? Yes, a fold of skin

indicators.note: Raised says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Asked whether it was raised by a crocodile, someone points to a flap of skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the hidden letters; 'Raised' turns them upwards in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The movable skin covering of the eye is a flap or fold of skin.

clue.text: Danger that must include sappers

indicators.note: include says the word 'that' takes the engineers inside it

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British army corps whose soldiers are called sappers

explanation.surface: A warning that some job will need the army's engineers.
explanation.walkthrough: Sappers are soldiers of the Royal Engineers, a British army corps; 'include' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A menace or likely source of harm is a danger.

clue.text: Sign first of reports in Spanish port

indicators.note: in puts that letter within the port's name

parts.note: Vigo is a port in north-west Spain

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A sign of the earliest reports coming out of a Spanish harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: The Virgin is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Police officer in precinct keeping quiet

indicators.note: keeping means the word for district holds the quiet letter

parts.note: a precinct is a district or sector
p, for piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A detective stays silent while in a police district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'precinct' sounds American and police-related, but here it means area; P goes inside SECTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A rank in the British police above sergeant, a detective title too, is a police officer.

clue.text: Mouse-like creature, wily, no end

indicators.note: no end means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: shrewd means canny or wily

explanation.surface: A cunning little rodent-like animal with an endless appetite.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny insect-eating mammal with a long snout resembles a mouse.

clue.text: Irritable Dickens character coming back to collect six shillings

indicators.note: to collect means the reversed name gathers the other letters inside it
coming back means the name reads backwards

parts.note: Uriah Heep is the scheming clerk in David Copperfield
VI is six in Roman numerals
s was the abbreviation for shillings in old British money

explanation.surface: A grumpy Dickensian figure returns to pick up a small debt in old money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns HEEP into PEEH, which takes VIS inside. The shilling was a pre-1971 British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tetchy and easily annoyed is bad-tempered, readily irritated.

clue.text: Sherry in a musty room's old

indicators.note: musty suggests something gone stale and off, so the letters of the word are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: An old sherry kept in a stale-smelling cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'musty' turns ROOMS into MOROS; the S of room's is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A medium-sweet, darkened form of oloroso from Spain is a style of sherry.
